## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Structured tool selection is a bounded, recognized model task.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Demonstrates constrained structured generation and evaluator design. |
| **Systems behavior** | Schema-heavy prefill and short structured decode. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | BFCL supplies data, evaluator, categories, and leaderboard. |
| **Model choice** | Qwen3-1.7B is an official Apache-2.0 checkpoint that fits laptop memory and has a strong published BFCL category score. |
| **Dataset choice** | Non-Live AST is an official bounded BFCL category that avoids web, memory, and external-service dependencies while retaining all 1,150 category examples. |
| **Quality metric** | The official AST evaluator and published aggregate avoid project-defined string matching. |
| **Published baseline** | 0.8292 Non-Live AST summary in the current official BFCL V4 Qwen3-1.7B function-calling leaderboard entry |
| **Alternative rejected** | Open-ended tool agents and custom prompts are unstable scaffolds. |

## Authoritative Sources and Adaptation

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Authority** | Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard and Qwen |
| **Model** | [open source](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B) |
| **Evaluator** | [open source](https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/tree/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard) |

**Adaptation boundary:** The max runner uses pinned Transformers for laptop inference, reproduces BFCL's Qwen FC prompt and parser, scores all six complete categories with the byte-pinned official AST checker, and applies the official equal-weight Non-Live AST aggregation.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload function-calling --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Candidate Quality Target

| **Field** | **Value** |

| **Target** | 0.8292 |
| **Direction** | higher |
| **Target kind** | published reference reproduction |
| **Target basis** | literature |
| **Tolerance** | 0.0 |
| **Reference runs** | 0 |

**Reviewer notes:**

- The target is the official BFCL V4 Qwen3-1.7B Non-Live AST summary. - The max runner binds all 1,150 cases, exact model bytes, the official Qwen FC prompt and parser, and the official AST checker. - The deterministic evaluator self-check retains three known Java representation exceptions; they do not remove tasks from model scoring. - The complete 1,150-case Apple MPS result scored 0.7852083333333333 under the pinned evaluator, so it is evidence for an honest target miss rather than a reason to relax the target.

## Results

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload function-calling --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.

**Backend rationale:** The pinned Transformers checkpoint supports CPU, CUDA, and Apple MPS execution.
